subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 8: Skills – Listening, speaking and writing a report
outcomes: I can ask and answer about a visit: Where did you go? What did you see there?
I can find the parts of a report: the date, paragraphs and headings.
I can plan, write and check a report about a visit.

tf.s: Osama's report is about the Louvre Abu Dhabi.
tf.why: Yes! Osama went to the Louvre Abu Dhabi.

tf.s: The Louvre Abu Dhabi has around 70 paintings.
A report about a visit starts with the date.
tf.why: Right! The date tells the reader when the visit happened.

tf.s: A report is written in one long line with no paragraphs.
We use an exclamation mark for interesting facts.
tf.why: Yes! I learnt a lot about Oman's past!

tf.s: The Louvre Abu Dhabi building is old and dark.
tf.why: It is very modern and beautiful, with lots of light.

tf.s: "Where did you go?" asks about a place you visited.
tf.why: Yes! It asks about the place.

tf.s: "Did you saw the doctor yesterday?" is correct.
tf.why: After did, use the base verb: Did you see …?

tf.s: "What did you learn?" is one of the report headings.
tf.why: Great! The report ends with what you learnt.

tf.s: The past simple of carry is carryed.

boxes.why: His report is about the Louvre Abu Dhabi.

boxes.q: About how many paintings does it have?

boxes.why: Past question: Where did you go?

boxes.q: Why does a report start with the date?
o: to tell the reader when the visit happened

boxes.q: "On 23 June, I visited the British Museum." Which heading?
o: When and where did you go?
boxes.why: It gives the date and the place.

boxes.q: Which punctuation mark do we use for interesting facts?
I learnt a lot ___ Oman's history.
My brother ___ Science last year. (not study)
Which is a place from the listening?
boxes.why: The places are the zoo, Science Museum, Car Museum and funfair.

hunt.q: Paintings at the Louvre Abu Dhabi
A place with rides and games

mcq.q: What is special about the Louvre Abu Dhabi?
o: The building is very modern and beautiful, with lots of light.
It is a small traditional house.
mcq.why: Osama's report describes a modern building with lots of light.

mcq.q: Which are the four report headings?
o: When and where? What's special? What could you do? What did you learn?
Who? What's he like? Where's he from? How old?
mcq.why: These are the parts of a report about a visit.

mcq.q: Which places are in the listening?
o: zoo, Science Museum, Car Museum, funfair

mcq.q: Which questions ask about a visit?
o: Where did you go? What did you see there?
How much is it? Can I help you?
mcq.why: These ask about a past visit.

mcq.q: Write the first sentence of a report with a date.
o: On Saturday 3 July, I visited the Natural History Museum of Oman.
mcq.why: Start with the date and the place, with capital letters.

mcq.q: Which plan notes are best for a report?
o: Bait Al Zubair – traditional house – saw old swords – learnt about Oman's past
mcq.why: The notes answer where, what's special, what you saw and what you learnt.

mcq.q: Write the "What's special about it?" sentence.
o: It's special because you can see a real whale.
mcq.why: It's special because … tells what is special.

mcq.q: Why does a report about a visit start with the date?
o: To tell the reader when the visit happened.
Because the date is a heading for what you learnt.

mcq.q: Find the mistake: "Did you saw the doctor yesterday?"
mcq.why: After did, use the base verb.

mcq.q: "I learnt a lot about Oman's past!" Which heading does this sentence go under?
o: When and where did you go?
